Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and appreciate the walkthrough of your search/QA use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary (from today's call)
- Primary workloads: customer support search + fraud signal enrichment (short text, 64-512 tokens typical)
- Goals: low-latency reranking for results returned to UI; consistent logging/tracing for audit and latency SLAs; secure auth for production keys

Integration + architecture items we agreed to follow up on
1) SDK setup & auth
   - You'd like guidance on OAuth (OIDC token exchange) vs API keys for server-side calls, and refresh flows for short-lived tokens.
2) Routing and model variants
   - Routing policy: latency-sensitive routes should hit smaller quantized models; archival/expensive quality routes can go to higher-accuracy variants.
3) Structured output / tool calling
   - We discussed function-style structured outputs for downstream extraction and deterministic tool triggers.
4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
   - Candidate retrieval (ANN) -> embed+rerank (batch embeddings + cross-encoder rerank if needed). Need to size for 10k qps spikes.
5) Observability hooks (priority)
   - Correlated trace IDs between FintechCo request and Redwood server processing
   - Logging fields: request_id, user_id, model_version, cache_hit, tokens_generated
   - Latency breakdown headers (e.g., X-Redwood-Latency, X-Redwood-KV-Cache, X-Redwood-Model-Inference) for downstream dashboards
   - Dashboards: per-route p50/p95 latency, tokens/call, cache-hit rate, and cost per request

Immediate next steps
- I've attached our integration checklist (redwood-integration-checklist.pdf) and a drive link with sample snippets.
- Monica to follow up with an SE deep-dive for auth & observability (Monica, looping you in).
- If you can share a sample request log (anonymized), we can map the trace ID correlation quickly.

Proposed times: Monica & I are available next Tue/Wed for a 60m deep-dive — let us know what works.

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our eng team (see inline):

1) Auth
- We prefer short-lived OAuth tokens from our identity provider (Auth0). Do you support an OIDC token exchange, or do we need to proxy API keys on our side?

2) Trace correlation
- We need to correlate our internal request_id with Redwood traces end-to-end. Is there a specific header you recommend we set (we typically set X-Request-ID) and will that map to a Redwood trace or is there an additional field we should expect back in responses?

3) Latency breakdown
- Can you confirm the header names you emit for per-stage latency so our gateway can log them? Also, are these available for both streaming and non-streaming responses?

4) Embeddings + reranker
- For rerank latency: what are realistic p95s for a cross-encoder rerank on 50 candidates for a 512-token context on a dedicated pool? If latency is too high we may prefer a hybrid approach (ANN + light reranker).

5) Structured output / tool calling
- We need to trigger internal tools based on structured function calls in streaming mode — do you support function/tool-calling in streaming and how do you surface incomplete/partial calls in the event of a stream cut?

Attached: sample request log (anonymized) — fintechco-request-log-sample.txt

Can Monica share a quick code snippet for header propagation and token exchange? Also happy to hop on the SE deep-dive next Tue afternoon.

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Great questions — below are the practical answers and a couple of snippets to get you unblocked quickly.

Auth / SDK support
- We support both API keys and OIDC-based short-lived tokens. Recommended pattern: Server-side exchange (your IDP -> backend) to get a short-lived Redwood token via our OIDC token exchange endpoint. That avoids long-lived keys on your servers.
- Flow: 1) Your backend gets IDP token (OIDC) -> 2) POST to https://api.redwood.inference/oidc/exchange with IDP token -> 3) Receive short-lived Redwood access_token (TTL configurable).

Header / trace correlation
- Set X-Request-ID for your internal tracing. Redwood will accept that header and return it verbatim in our response headers. Additionally, we attach X-Redwood-Trace: <trace-id> which is our internal trace id (useful for support & log joins). You can correlate by storing both. Example response headers we emit:
  - X-Redwood-Trace: rwd-trace-01c9a2b4
  - X-Redwood-Request-ID: <your X-Request-ID value>
  - X-Redwood-Latency: total=123ms;kv=12ms;model=98ms;overhead=13ms
  - X-Redwood-KV-Cache: hit

Streaming behavior
- Streaming supports function/tool calling. Partial/early function calls are emitted as structured events in the stream ("function_call.start", "function_call.args", "function_call.complete"). If a stream cuts, you will receive a final metadata event that includes call status and a truncated args flag.

Embeddings + reranker guidance
- For dedicated GPU pools with optimized kernels, a cross-encoder rerank of 50 candidates for ~512-token contexts typically falls in the 120-250ms p95 range (depends on model family & batch sizing).
- Hybrid recommendation: ANN for initial recall (sub-50ms), then small cross-encoder for top-K (K <= 20) to keep p95 under 150ms. We can provide a tuned quantized model for lower latency.

Code snippets (Python curl & python requests examples)
- Header propagation (curl):
  curl -X POST \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_TOKEN>" \\
    -H "X-Request-ID: $(uuidgen)" \\
    https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate

- Reading headers (Python requests):
  resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
  redwood_trace = resp.headers.get('X-Redwood-Trace')
  latency = resp.headers.get('X-Redwood-Latency')
